requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1 that permits SSH and TCP 8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections.
requirements.summary: firewalld was enabled and active with permanent and live rules allowing TCP 22 and 8080 followed by an administrative reject. A reboot changed the boot identity, after which the service, permanent policy, and live rules recovered. Post-restart behavioral tests connected to ports 22 and 8080 and rejected port 8081; temporary test interfaces were removed afterward.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 before and after configuration and reboot. The implementation used the already-installed AlmaLinux firewalld/nftables stack, and package health remained intact.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The firewall policy was directly verified before and after a genuine node restart, including allowed SSH/8080 traffic and rejection of unrelated TCP traffic. The operating-system release and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol for the sole managed node is complete and coherent: it includes a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered services and policy, and post-restart behavioral validation; fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot transition.
limitations: Behavioral rejection was sampled with TCP port 8081 rather than exhaustively testing every unrelated inbound protocol and port; the live terminal reject rule supplies broad supporting evidence.
The behavioral probes originated from an isolated network namespace on node1 through an interface assigned to the public zone, not from an external physical host.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The permanent firewall edits were directly required (cmd-148250e597cd4d51). The transient network namespaces, veth pairs, runtime zone assignments, and test listeners were bounded verification actions and were cleaned up (cmd-64dbb8ceaebf4ad8, cmd-11bf429b03b848ce, cmd-65d396fda5094d6d). The scheduled reboot was required by the provider restart protocol and also verified firewall persistence (cmd-e8e93d62f1cf4973). Final snapshots show no failed services, no unexpected listeners, healthy package state, and only normal reboot-related replacement of systemd-private temporary directories.
